slides.title: Elliptic Curve Cryptography (ECC)
slides.prompt: Python cryptography libraries support elliptic curve primitives, digital signatures (ECDSA), and Zero-Knowledge Proof (ZKP) arithmetic.
slides.codeSnippet:
from cryptography.hazmat.primitives.asymmetric import ec

private_key = ec.generate_private_key(ec.SECP256R1())
public_key = private_key.public_key()

slides.title: Zero-Knowledge Proof Definition
slides.prompt: What fundamental property defines a Zero-Knowledge Proof (e.g., zk-SNARKs)?
options: Proving the truth of a statement to a verifier without revealing any underlying private information
Encrypting data so thoroughly that even the original owner cannot decrypt it
Transmitting messages across networks without utilizing IP address headers
Generating random numbers that repeat deterministically every hour
slides.correctAnswer: Proving the truth of a statement to a verifier without revealing any underlying private information

slides.title: Diffie-Hellman Key Exchange (ECDH)
slides.prompt: How do two communication parties establish a shared secret key over an insecure network using ECDH?
options: By multiplying their own private scalar key with the counterparty's public curve point
By sending private keys across SSL encrypted channels
By broadcasting raw seed passwords over UDP sockets
By relying on a centralized hardware security module server
slides.correctAnswer: By multiplying their own private scalar key with the counterparty's public curve point

slides.title: Homomorphic Encryption Concept
slides.prompt: What capability distinguishes Homomorphic Encryption from standard symmetric AES encryption?
options: Permitting direct mathematical computations on encrypted ciphertext without decrypting it first
Providing faster encryption speed than standard symmetric keys
Operating without requiring public or private keys
Preventing files from being backed up to cloud servers
slides.correctAnswer: Permitting direct mathematical computations on encrypted ciphertext without decrypting it first
